commitMessage:
Use the module timestamp instead of the timestamp of the state object

Currently the state timestamp is used what can change if a bundle is
resolved not only when it is installed/updated/uninstalled, but the
Platform#getStateStamp() claims exactly this.

To restore the documented behavior this iterates over all bundles and
uses its Module#getTimestamp instead, this also removes the reference to
the  PlatformAdmin that currently requires the compatibility module and
could therefore be removed from this once we have migrated PDE.
summary: Adds `(forRemoval = true)` to `@Deprecated` annotations where applicable in Java 9+.

commitMessage:
Use a composite key of all bundle ids and version to check the cache

Currently the ContentDescriptionManager relies on a rather vague
"timestamp" to indicate that the set of bundles has changed, this leads
to some hard to explain instabilities in tests.

This now uses a composite key of all bundle ids and their version and
computes a hashsum from the string, this has the advantage that it is
deterministic what properties of a bundle set is compared.
dslRule:
<!id: merge.null.check.and.method.call.if>
<!description: Merges a null check `if` statement with a subsequent `if` statement that calls a method on the same variable, both leading to the exact same single statement outcome, into a single combined `if` statement. This is safe due to short-circuiting of the OR operator, preventing NullPointerExceptions.>
<!severity: HINT>

if ($var == null)
    $stmt;
if ($var.$method($args$))
    $stmt;
=>
if (($var == null) || $var.$method($args$))
    $stmt;
;;
dslValidationResult: Parse error at line 6: Expected '=>' or ';;' but found: $stmt; (line 6)

commitMessage:
[performance] do not normalize locations that are already normalized

When projects or links are added to the workspace the file location is
normalized and saved to disk. Good. However it is not needed to do that
for those already normalized paths that are loaded back from disk.

Saves some startup time on windows, where name capitalization of each
path segment is expensive IO.
dslRule:
<!id: project.internal.set_normalized_description>
<!description: Optimize internal project description setting by signaling pre-normalized location. Avoids redundant URI normalization when the location is known to be already normalized, typically when loaded from persistence. This improves startup performance.>
<!severity: HINT>
<!tags: performance, internal>

$project.internalSetDescription($description, false)
=>
$project.internalSetDescription($description, false, true)
;;
summary: Optimize internal project description setting by signaling pre-normalized location.

commitMessage:
SafeFileOutputStream: avoid touching files #1220

SafeFileOutputStream is used to write Workspace metadata on eclipse
exit. This did touch the existing files even when the content stayed the
same. With this change the content is prepared in a byte array and
flushed to disk if and only if the content changed.

https://github.com/eclipse-platform/eclipse.platform/issues/1220
summary: Internal refactoring of I/O mechanism in SafeFileOutputStream, not expressible as a simple DSL cleanup.

commitMessage:
Updated bundles with comparator errors

See: eclipse-platform/eclipse.platform.releng.aggregator#1923

Disable auto-save action for combining if statements

The rule of having only a single if statement instead of fall-throughs
is not followed at several places in the code and leads to unintended
changes when saving the according files, e.g., moving an if statement
away from the explaining comment. This change disables the auto-save
action for all platform projects.
summary: The commit disables a problematic Eclipse JDT cleanup option that combines sequential if statements with fall-through blocks, as it caused unintended stylistic changes in code.

commitMessage:
Simplify lambda expression and method reference syntax

Applies the cleanup action to simplify lambda expression and method
reference syntax in all projects to conform to defined save actions.
This includes the following:
* replace simple method calls in lambda expressions by method references
* remove unnecessary parentheses around lambda input argument
dslRule:
<!id: lambda.simplify.singleParamParens>
<!description: Remove unnecessary parentheses around a single lambda input argument.
This is a stylistic change that does not alter semantics.>
<!severity: HINT>
<!minJavaVersion: 8>

($param$) -> $body
=> $param -> $body
;;
summary: Simplifies single-parameter lambda expressions by removing redundant parentheses around the argument.
